review: Chapter text reviewed. Each sample family and eligible ability membership is enumerated separately. Underlying trait procedures and countermeasure definitions remain cross-reference obligations; no runtime power is claimed implemented.

entries.acceptance: Campaign configuration declares whether mental powers exist, eligible origins and any required background cost; reject disallowed purchases before spending points.
A power definition has an explicit ability membership list, source modifier and talent policy; missing required fields or conflicting definitions cannot silently use defaults from another power.
entries.validation_note: Power definition, owned talent pricing, pure bonus and latent eligibility authored; fixtures unrun. Actual ability effects, roll dispatch, purchases and interference remain pending.

entries.acceptance: Acquiring the first ability or talent in an unrelated power after creation requires a specific campaign permission or authored transformation event; existing power membership grants no blanket access.
The campaign identifies limitations intrinsic to its powers; ability customization and later advancement must preserve these restrictions.
An authored permission names which nonfundamental limitations practice may remove; apply the resulting point difference and effect changes once.
Permit an authored replacement or extension of a sample power's ability membership, with explicit countermeasure and talent rules and a reason when an ability is rejected.
Require an explicit authored talent price for unusually broad powers rather than silently applying the ordinary five-point rate.
entries.validation_note: Power definition, owned talent pricing, pure bonus and latent eligibility authored; fixtures unrun. Actual ability effects, roll dispatch, purchases and interference remain pending.

entries.acceptance: Define the campaign's living/sentient eligibility policy for thought-based powers; attempts against recordings or inert replicas fail under the normal policy without affecting those objects.

An authored information resolver receives outcome quality and relevant world facts, returns constrained useful information on success, no information on ordinary failure, and misleading information on specified severe failures; keep hidden rolls out of player-visible diagnostics.
Possessing at least one ability establishes membership in its associated power; talent alone represents latent access, not an active ability.
A character with a power's talent but no abilities can buy an eligible first ability within that power using earned points.
entries.validation_note: Power definition, owned talent pricing, pure bonus and latent eligibility authored; fixtures unrun. Actual ability effects, roll dispatch, purchases and interference remain pending.

entries.acceptance: A character with an existing power can buy new eligible abilities, higher ability levels, enhancements and its talent using one advancement ledger.
A partially purchased potential ability remains subject to both unconscious-only and uncontrollable behavior until fully paid; it does not provide ordinary voluntary activation.
Preserve the underlying trait's activation, duration, resistance, resource costs and effects; adding a power modifier must not replace these with a universal activation roll or generic duration.
The power modifier makes an ability vulnerable to its applicable power-wide and all-power interference in addition to ordinary specific countermeasures.

Add the associated talent level to rolls to activate or use that power, including applicable intelligence, will and perception rolls; do not add the bonus twice when an ability delegates to another module.
entries.validation_note: Power definition, owned talent pricing, pure bonus and latent eligibility authored; fixtures unrun. Actual ability effects, roll dispatch, purchases and interference remain pending.

entries.acceptance: Allow ability possession without talent and talent without ability; talent does not supply missing abilities or additional effect magnitude by itself.
entries.validation_note: Power definition, owned talent pricing, pure bonus and latent eligibility authored; fixtures unrun. Actual ability effects, roll dispatch, purchases and interference remain pending.

entries.acceptance: Ordinary talents cost five points per level and normally stop at four; exceeding four requires a specific campaign permission.
entries.validation_note: Power definition, owned talent pricing, pure bonus and latent eligibility authored; fixtures unrun. Actual ability effects, roll dispatch, purchases and interference remain pending.

entries.acceptance: Support levels of one ability with different extra limitations while retaining the power modifier on every level; activation can use only levels whose individual conditions are satisfied.
Reject removal of the power modifier or a campaign-fundamental limitation through ordinary advancement, even when the character can afford the unmodified ability.
Apply mental-power resistance to permitted resistance rolls for direct and area targets; it does not create a resistance roll for an unresisted effect.
entries.validation_note: Owned resistance pricing and IQ/Will check contexts authored, including immunity/no-resistance suppression of rolls; fixtures unrun. Full ability contest and countermeasure integration remain pending.

entries.acceptance: Delegate neutralization to its trait procedure and ongoing state while selecting only powers affected by that countermeasure; successful suppression cannot delete paid ability investments.
Resolve static interference using its trait rules and scope, including passive suppression, without adding an unrelated activation cost.
Technological or other specifically authored countermeasures affect their named powers only; an ordinary mind shield cannot automatically suppress every power family.
The counterpower family has neither its own talent nor a source discount, and its abilities cannot themselves be blocked by mental-power interference.
Keep extrasensory information rolls secret; success quality controls information usefulness and ordinary failure yields no information.
For object-history and future-sensing abilities, failure by more than five produces false information; failure by exactly five and failures of other abilities do not inherit this rule.
Matter-control talent also modifies applicable dexterity rolls, including attack accuracy and flight maneuvers, without increasing damage dice or speed.

A thought-family affliction or innate attack requires the resisted-curse enhancement and effects limited to fatigue, stun, incapacitation, temporary mental disadvantages or dexterity/intelligence/will penalties.
Magic detection and anti-mental-power suppression distinguish origins; shared physical outcomes can interact without reclassifying their source.
A physically produced flame can be extinguished by an appropriate spell, and a mental shield can resist a mind-reading spell when its underlying rules apply.
Mental abilities do not automatically inherit spell rituals, mana requirements, time or energy costs; only their own traits and limitations impose those restrictions.
For an authored power, use a -10% source modifier when the declared countermeasure model meets this case: Common countermeasures include both neutralization and static interference variants.
For an authored power, use a -5% source modifier when the declared countermeasure model meets this case: Common countermeasures exist but lack those broad blocking variants.
For an authored power, use a 0% source modifier when the declared countermeasure model meets this case: Countermeasures are rare; do not grant a limitation discount.
If no countermeasures exist, use the applicable cosmic enhancement rather than a limitation discount; verify its actual trait pricing and permitted effects.
